title: How to Send a Large Money Transfer to India for Diwali 2026
summary: Planning a large Diwali transfer to India? Learn how exchange rates, limits, and documents affect sending $10,000+ from the U.S. ahead of November 8, 2026.
body_markdown:
***Quick answer:** Diwali 2026 falls on November 8, so plan large transfers to India at least one to two weeks ahead. Compare exchange rates and fees, confirm transfer limits with your provider, and have identification ready, since larger amounts often require extra verification. Remitly offers multiple delivery options and support for qualifying transfers of $5,000 or more through Remitly Concierge.*


**[Diwali is one of the most meaningful times of the year](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/celebrating-diwali/) for Indian families spread across the United States and India** . Beyond diyas, sweets, and gatherings, it’s also a peak season for money moving home. Inbound remittances to India typically rise in the weeks around the festival, as Indian Americans and NRIs send larger-than-usual amounts for a gift for parents, support for a sibling’s wedding, or a contribution toward a family project.


[Many also send money for Dhanteras](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/dhanteras-dates-and-gold-buying-traditions/) , the first day of Diwali, when buying gold is considered auspicious and families traditionally purchase gold, silver, or new utensils for the year ahead.


[Sending a large amount of money internationally](https://www.remitly.com/us/en/money-transfer/large-amounts) is different from sending a routine transfer. Exchange rates matter more, fees can add up, and your provider may ask for additional documentation before releasing the funds. Planning ahead helps you avoid last-minute stress and makes sure your money arrives when your family needs it most.


This guide walks through what to expect when sending $5,000, $10,000, or more from the U.S. to India ahead of Diwali 2026, including how exchange rates work, what documents you might need, and how to get more value from your transfer.


## When is Diwali in 2026?


Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, falls on **November 8, 2026** . The festival typically spans five days, with celebrations and gift-giving often beginning in the days leading up to the main event.


Because Diwali is a fixed cultural touchpoint each year, it’s also a predictable time for increased demand on money transfer services. Sending money a week or two in advance of November 8 helps avoid the bottlenecks that can happen when many senders are transferring at once.


### Why timing matters for large transfers


Banks in India are typically closed for part of the Diwali holidays, and closures vary by state. Bank deposits may not post until banks reopen, so a transfer sent right before the festival could reach your family later than expected. Sending a few days early helps your money arrive in time for Dhanteras and Diwali shopping. Mobile wallet and other delivery options may not depend on bank hours, so ask your family what works best for them.


## Why send a large amount of money to India for Diwali?


For many Indian American families, Diwali is as much a financial occasion as it is a cultural one. Common reasons for sending larger transfers around this time include:


- **Gold and Dhanteras purchases:** Dhanteras, the first day of Diwali, is considered the most auspicious day of the year to buy gold, silver, or new utensils. Many senders fund these purchases for family in India, or send money so parents can buy gold on their behalf as a gift or long-term savings.
- **Family gifts:** Supporting parents, grandparents, or siblings with a meaningful monetary gift for the festival.
- **Wedding or event contributions:** Diwali season often overlaps with[wedding season in India](https://www.remitly.com/blog/lifestyle-culture/wedding-traditions-in-india/) , prompting larger one-time transfers.
- **Investments or property payments:** Some senders use the holiday period to make progress on family investments,[such as land](https://www.remitly.com/blog/money-transfer/how-to-fund-a-property-closing-in-india-from-the-us/) , renovations, or **[education expenses](https://www.remitly.com/blog/money-transfer/how-to-pay-tuition-in-india-from-the-us/)** .
- **Charitable giving:** Diwali is associated with generosity, and many families choose this time to support charitable causes back home.


Whatever the reason, sending a larger sum means it’s worth taking a bit more time to understand how exchange rates, fees, and transfer limits will affect what your recipient actually receives.


## How to send a large amount of money from the U.S. to India for Diwali


Sending money from the U.S. to India doesn’t have to be complicated, but a few extra steps are worth taking when the amount is significant.


### Step 1: Choose a licensed money transfer provider


Look for a provider that is licensed and regulated in the U.S., such as a money transmitter registered with[FinCEN](https://www.fincen.gov/) and licensed in your state. This protects your funds and gives you legal recourse if something goes wrong.


### Step 2: Compare exchange rates and fees side by side


[The USD-to-INR exchange rate](https://www.remitly.com/us/en/currency-converter/usd-to-inr-rate) fluctuates daily, and even small differences can affect how much your recipient gets, especially on larger transfers. Some providers advertise a lower fee but offer a less favorable exchange rate, so it’s worth comparing the total amount your recipient will receive rather than just the headline fee.


### Step 3: Confirm the transfer limit and verification requirements


Most providers set daily, monthly, or per-transaction limits, which can vary based on your account history, verification level, and the provider’s own policies. If you’re sending $10,000 or more, check your provider’s specific limit before you start, since you may need to complete additional verification first.


### Step 4: Choose your funding and delivery method


You’ll typically be able to fund your transfer using a U.S. bank account, debit card, or sometimes a credit card, though fees may differ by method. On the delivery side, many providers offer options like direct bank deposit, mobile wallet transfer, cash pickup, or home delivery in India, depending on where your recipient lives.


### Step 5: Submit the transfer and track it


Once you’ve entered the recipient’s details and confirmed the amount, you can submit the transfer. Most digital providers, including Remitly, let you[track the transfer’s status in real time](https://www.remitly.com/blog/money-transfer/how-to-track-your-money-transfer-with-the-remitly-app/) through their app or website.

## What to know before sending $10,000 or more to India


Sending a large amount comes with a few considerations that smaller transfers don’t typically involve.


### Why might my provider ask for extra documentation?


Financial institutions are required to follow[anti-money laundering (AML) regulations](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/aml) , which means larger transfers often trigger additional[identity or source-of-funds verification](https://www.remitly.com/blog/finance/types-of-identification-documents/) . This is standard practice across the industry, not a sign of a problem with your transfer.


### What documents might I need?


Depending on the provider and the size of your transfer, you may be asked to provide:


- A government-issued photo ID (such as a passport or driver’s license)
- Proof of address
- Documentation showing the source of funds, such as a pay stub, bank statement, or sale document
- Additional information about the purpose of the transfer


Requirements vary by provider and transfer amount, so it’s a good idea to check what’s needed before you begin, especially if you’re sending close to a deadline like Diwali.


### Are there limits on how much I can send?


Yes. **[Transfer limits](https://www.remitly.com/us/en/landing/send-limits)** vary by provider, your verification level, and sometimes by destination country regulations in India. Rather than assuming a specific number, check your provider’s current limits directly, as they can change over time.


## How to get more value when sending a large amount to India


A large transfer magnifies the impact of even small differences in exchange rates and fees. A few strategies can help:


### Compare the total amount received, not just the fee


Some providers highlight a “$0 fee” offer but build their margin into a less competitive exchange rate. When comparing options, look at the final INR amount your recipient will receive, not just the advertised fee.


### Understand promotional exchange rates


Some providers offer a promotional exchange rate for new customers or for a limited portion of your transfer. It’s worth reading the fine print, since a promotional rate may apply only to the first transfer or to a capped amount, with the standard rate applying beyond that threshold.


### Consider the hypothetical impact of rate differences


Here’s a simplified example to illustrate why comparing rates matters on larger transfers:


**Exchange rate (USD to INR)** **Amount sent** **Approximate INR received**


96.00 $10,000 ₹960,000


95.50 $10,000 ₹995,000


This hypothetical example shows how a difference of just half a rupee per dollar can mean ₹5,000 more or less for your recipient on a $10,000 transfer. Actual rates change daily, so always check the current rate before sending.


### Time your transfer thoughtfully


Exchange rates move throughout the day and across weeks. While no one can predict currency markets with certainty, keeping an eye on the USD-to-INR rate over a few days before Diwali can help you choose a moment that feels right for your transfer.

## Tips for sending money to India before Diwali 2026


- **Start early.** Begin the process at least one to two weeks before November 8 to allow time for any additional verification.
- **Gather your documents in advance.** Having ID, proof of address, and source-of-funds documentation ready can speed up a larger transfer.
- **Check current exchange rates and limits.** Rates and limits change, so verify them close to the time you plan to send.
- **Choose the right delivery method for your recipient.** Ask your family member in India which delivery option works best for them.
- **Keep a record of your transfer confirmation.** This is useful if you need to follow up on delivery status.


## Frequently asked questions about Diwali money transfers


### What is the best way to send a large amount of money to India for Diwali?


The best approach is to compare licensed providers based on the total amount your recipient will receive after fees and exchange rates, confirm transfer limits and documentation requirements in advance, and choose a delivery method that works for your recipient, such as bank deposit or mobile wallet.


### How much does it cost to send $10,000 to India?


Costs vary by provider and depend on the funding method, delivery method, and current exchange rate. Rather than a fixed cost, it’s best to check the fee and exchange rate for your specific transfer amount directly with your provider before sending.


### How long does it take to send money from the U.S. to India?


Delivery times vary based on the provider, funding method, delivery method, and whether additional verification is needed for larger amounts. Check the estimated delivery window with your provider at the time you initiate the transfer.


### Do I need to provide documents to send a large amount of money?


For larger transfers, many providers require identity verification and may request documentation about the source of funds. This is a standard regulatory requirement across the money transfer industry, not specific to any one provider.

Cross-border transfers can have tax or reporting implications depending on your personal circumstances and the laws of both the US and India. This article does not provide individualized tax advice, so consult a qualified tax professional for guidance specific to your situation.
